title: smoothquant lane balancer + kernel slew-rate limiter to stabilize INT8/FP8 hotpaths
author: Aisha Malik
description:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent latency spikes and throughput jitter on INT8/FP8 serving paths for mixed-length chat workloads. Root cause analysis showed that bursts of requests targeting smoothquant-enabled model variants created transient imbalances across execution lanes, which in turn caused frequent kernel thrashing (rapid kernel load/unload cycles) and increased GPU kernel launch overhead. Additionally, KV-cache eviction patterns were amplified when lanes switched execution contexts rapidly, reducing effective KV-hit-rate for conversational workloads. This PR introduces two coordinated subsystems: (1) a lane balancer that enforces longer-lived lane affinity for smoothquant/quantized hotpaths and (2) a kernel slew-rate limiter that smooths the rate at which high-cost quant kernels are scheduled onto devices.

Design summary: - Lane Balancer: new scheduler component that assigns incoming requests to execution lanes with knowledge of quantization variant (INT8/FP8/smoothquant), sequence length distribution, and recent KV-cache residency. Balancer favors sticky affinity for lanes that currently hold compatible KV cache entries and that have low recent kernel-change frequency. The balancer is parameterized (decay windows, affinity threshold) so we can tune for latency vs. cache locality. - Kernel Slew-Rate Limiter: a lightweight token-bucket-like regulator applied to high-latency quant kernels (dequant fusion + smoothquant postprocessing). Instead of unbounded immediate scheduling, the limiter enforces a configurable ramp-up allowing the scheduler to batch or coalesce small bursts into fewer kernel launches while respecting latency SLOs. The limiter interacts with continuous batching so microbatch sizes are adjusted when the limiter is active. - KV affinity hints: runtime now propagates a per-request KV-affinity hint from the scheduler to the executor so that lane assignment considers cache residency and avoids cross-lane eviction churn. - Telemetry and knobs: exposed runtime flags and console metrics: lane_affinity_hits, kernel_slew_backpressure, lane_switch_count, avg_kernel_launchs_per_sec.

Implementation notes: - Added runtime/scheduler/lane_balancer.{cc,h} implementing the balancing policy and a small state table per lane. - Added runtime/kernel/slew_limiter.{cc,h} which instruments kernel scheduling API and integrates with the continuous-batcher to optionally increase microbatch window. - Extended executor to accept kv_affinity_hint and to annotate lane metadata used by the balancer. - Tests: unit tests for lane balancing heuristics and integration perf tests that simulate mixed-length chat traffic using the perf harness. - Backwards compatibility: flags default to conservative values (balancer off for legacy deployments) and the limiter is initially permissive; both are configurable via rollout feature gates.

Checklist: - [x] Core balancer implementation - [x] Slew limiter implementation - [x] Unit tests for heuristics - [x] Integration performance tests - [x] Console metrics and basic docs - [x] Coordinated rollout plan and feature flags

Commits summary: "a6f4e3: runtime: add lane balancer core; b9c23d: runtime: kernel slew limiter and scheduler hook; d4f7ab: executor: accept kv_affinity_hint and annotate lanes; e1532d: perf: add mixed-length benchmark harness; f8b1c2: tests: unit tests for balancer and limiter; ff9e11: docs: console metrics and rollout notes"

Changed files (high level): "runtime/scheduler/lane_balancer.cc, runtime/scheduler/lane_balancer.h, runtime/kernel/slew_limiter.cc, runtime/kernel/slew_limiter.h, runtime/executor/kv_affinity.h, runtime/executor/affinity_integration.cc, runtime/tests/perf_smoothquant_bench.cc, docs/perf_notes/smoothquant_lane_balancer.md, pkg/flags/feature_gates.go"

Testing and benchmarks: "We ran end-to-end benchmarks on a mixed-length chat workload (OpenLLaMA-7B smoothquant variant) across multiple instance types (g4dn.12xlarge, p3.8xlarge). Key results (median of 5 runs): - g4dn.12xlarge: p50 latency +1% (within noise), p95 latency -8%, p99 latency -12%, overall throughput +8% at 95th percentile tail target, average token cost reduction ~6% due to higher KV-hit-rate and reduced kernel-launch overhead. - p3.8xlarge: p99 latency -10%, throughput +5%. Additional microbench: with artificial burst traffic (200 concurrent short requests), kernel_slew_backpressure prevented a 2.5x kernel-launch increase and reduced GPU occupancy variance by ~30%." 

Observability: added console charts for lane_affinity_hits and kernel_slew_backpressure and traced example sessions showing reduced lane_switch_count. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flags (done). - Canary on dedicated capacity for two customers with mixed chat workloads (scheduled week 1 post-merge). - Gradual ramp to 25% of production dedicated clusters with monitoring alerts on lane_switch_count and p99 latency (week 2-3). - Full enablement conditional on alarms and no regression after 2 weeks. Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current affinity hint is coarse-grained; follow-up (ENG-1450) will propagate per-layer KV residency signals to further reduce eviction. - Slew limiter currently uses static token-bucket params per model family; future work to autotune based on live SLOs is tracked separately. - Edge cases: long-running large-batch workloads may disable the balancer for those lanes; logic in place to detect and opt-out but more tests planned.

Release notes (short): "Stability/perf: Add smoothquant lane balancing and kernel slew-rate limiter to reduce INT8/FP8 kernel thrash and improve tail latency for mixed-length chat workloads. Off by default; opt-in via feature gate."

perf_summary: p99 latency reduced by 10-12% on typical GPU instance types for mixed-length workloads; throughput improved by 5-8%; token unit cost reduced by ~6% in our benchmarks due to improved KV hit locality and fewer kernel launches.
release_notes: Add lane balancing and kernel slew-rate limiting for smoothquant/int8 paths to reduce tail latency and stabilize throughput. Feature gated and off by default; canary rollout recommended.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in default config to minimize risk. Follow-ups tracked: ENG-1450 (per-layer KV hints), ENG-1461 (autotune slew parameters).
